ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act of Korea, Act No. 1000, as amended, Articles 289, 330 and 635; Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information, Act No. 6516, as amended, Articles 2 and 5-3 and its Enforcement Decree; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality, Act No. 5493, as amended; Regulations on Customer Identification and Due Diligence under the Financial Information and Reporting System; FATF Recommendation 24 as implemented by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry Office of the competent District Court under the Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic Korean registry extract requires no apostille or consular legalization for use in Korea; for cross-border use, the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs issues the Hague Apostille only if the destination state is party to the 1961 Convention, with consular legalization used only for non-Hague destination states. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and are never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Korean Registered Matters Certificate and Tax Clearance Confirmation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local District Court Registry and Korea National Tax Service
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: When obtained from the origin country as a foreign document, the issuing country's competent authority must issue a Hague Apostille if the issuing country is an Apostille Convention member; if the issuing country is a non-member, the Korean Embassy or Consulate in that country must perform consular legalization. The two routes are parallel and exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the foreign corporate shareholder and a Korean Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The executed resolution and PoA must be notarized at the place of execution, then sealed with a Hague Apostille by the competent authority of an Apostille Convention state; if executed in a non-Hague state, Korean consular legalization replaces the apostille but is never added to an already apostilled document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean notary public and the incorporating shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The original Korean articles are prepared and notarized in Korea and ordinarily require no foreign legalization; for any foreign exhibit, obtain a Hague Apostille from the exhibit's country if an Apostille member, otherwise Korean consular legalization; never both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter or Financial Capacity Confirmation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Parent company bank or target operating bank in Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: A bank officer's signed reference with bank seal is processed, when required by a receiving Korean bank, through either a Hague Apostille of the bank's home state or, for non-Hague states, through Korean consular legalization of the notarized bank signature; not both sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening applies at onboarding and continuously to all shareholders, directors, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit sanctions and watchlist registry, UN Security Council consolidated and targeted sanctions lists, U.S. OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions, and relevant Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Financial Services Commission designations. PEPs, including members of any foreign legislative, judicial, or military body, must be identified through a risk-based test and a 18-month cooling-off review after leaving office, with enhanced due diligence on source of wealth and source of funds. Customer due diligence files must contain beneficial ownership information at the 25% threshold, be updated annually or upon any control change, and be retained according to statutory document retention periods. For every high-risk transaction, a written suspicious transaction report to the Korea FIU is required within three days of reasonable suspicion.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Registry and Corporation Search Portal (i-Registry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be stated in the Korean national script (Hangul); a Latin-alphabet trade name may be separately registered only as a trade name. The registry applies a phonetic-transliteration rule when the proposed name is derived from a foreign-language word, and requires the four-tier company-type designation to appear expressly in the corporate name, being Chusik Hoesa, Yuhan Hoesa, Hapja Hoesa, or Hapmyeong Hoesa for stock, limited liability, limited partnership, and unlimited partnership forms respectively.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the registry judge gives a written statement of objection. The applicant has 14 days to file a written appeal with the same district registry office, stating legal grounds and attaching evidence of distinguishability, prior consent, or the absence of public deception. If that appeal fails, the applicant may bring an immediate appeal to the appellate court under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act; a simultaneous repair filing with a new distinctive token is permitted, but it opens a new clearance window rather than extending the original reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure commercial mailbox or a virtual office without a physical, identifiable and controllable workspace will be rejected by the Korean tax authorities, registrar, and commercial banks. For an ERP/CRM vertical cloud company, the tax authority requires a real business place for VAT registration and electronic tax invoice issuance; bank account opening requires a lease agreement in the corporate name and proof of the subscribed service capacity. A serviced-office virtual address is permissible only if it provides a dedicated desk or meeting room, mail handling, a visible space, and is not a mass-registration accommodation; the registered address must correspond to actual decision-making and record-keeping.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: original lease contract; deposit or utility payment invoice; evidence of employees or independent director presence; network or cloud-service logs; corporate signboard; VAT invoice issuing records. Quantified risk: low to moderate, approximately 10-15% annual inspection probability for a standard-risk cloud software company with one physical office; if the address appears on an investigated mass-registration list, the probability rises above 40% and will likely trigger a court or tax investigation before incorporation approval.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), particularly Articles 289 (Articles of Incorporation), 292 (Notarization of Articles), 295 (Subscription of Shares at Incorporation), 305 (Payment of Subscription Price), 306 (Election of Directors at Incorporation), 309 (Registration of Incorporation), and 312 (Effect of Incorporation Registration); supplemented by the Registration of Real Estate and Registration of Corporation Matters Rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Legal Registration Division, Local District Court under the Supreme Court Registration Office (Court Administration Office); jurisdiction determined by the registered office of the Chusik Hoesa.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Corporation Registration (Beobin Deunggi Production Certificate / Beobindunggi Tonji) issued after formal filing of the Application for Establishment Registration of a Corporation (Beobin Seollip Deunggi Sincheongseo).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None: Korean law does not currently prescribe a fixed statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa. Incorporators may set a nominal share capital in the Articles of Incorporation. However, before filing incorporation registration, the entire subscription price must be deposited into a designated bank subscription account or secured by a bank guarantee in accordance with Article 305 of the Korean Commercial Act. No post-registration blocked escrow account is required; the subscribed funds become corporate assets upon registration.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea; electronic registration and compliance portal: HomeTax (https://www.hometax.go.kr), together with Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS for export clearance declarations
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a domestic Chusik Hoesa, the statutory tax identification process begins with incorporation in the Korean Commercial Registry. The representative director files the Business Registration application with the competent District Tax Office within 20 days from the commencement of business, using the Korean corporate registration number, articles of incorporation, certificate of incorporation, corporate seal certificate, evidence of Korean business premises, and director identification documents. The NTS then issues the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which functions as both the corporate TIN and the VAT registration number. For a foreign non-resident entity that is not incorporated in Korea but is subject to Korean VAT registration for cross-border electronic services, the foreign entity must, electronically via HomeTax or through a properly appointed domestic tax representative, submit a Business Registration application accompanied by the foreign certificate of incorporation, charter or equivalent constitutive document, board resolution, power of attorney appointing a Korean tax representative, and any additional evidence that the entity has economic activity triggering Korean tax registration. The NTS will then issue a Korean tax identification number allocated to the non-resident business operator.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; Korea does not maintain a check-the-box election equivalent to the US regime. A Chusik Hoesa is automatically taxable as a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act on worldwide income, and hybrid mismatch rules under the International Tax Adjustment Act restrict the effectiveness of hybrid entity structuring.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: General VAT registration under the Korean VAT Act has no monetary turnover threshold; every taxable business must register within 20 days from commencement. The KRW 80,000,000 annual taxable supply threshold identifies eligibility for simplified taxpayer treatment for very small domestic businesses. For foreign non-resident suppliers of electronically supplied digital services to Korean unregistered customers, mandatory Korean VAT registration is triggered when the annual taxable supply to Korean consumers exceeds the statutory overseas e-commerce supplier threshold prescribed under the VAT Act Enforcement Decree, currently set at KRW 50,000,000, or when a designated domestic tax representative or withholding arrangement is otherwise required.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT taxpayers are required to issue Korean tax invoices and transmit electronic tax invoices through the NTS HomeTax e-tax invoice system. Electronic tax invoices must be submitted to the NTS within the statutory filing timeline after supply, and ERP systems can interface with HomeTax through structured API/ME-based batch transmission channels authorized by the NTS. Korea operates a national centralized e-tax invoice data repository rather than a third-party pre-clearance or fiscal stamping system; the NTS uses real-time data intake for anti-fraud cross-matching of tax invoices, trade transactions, and VAT returns.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exported tangible goods qualify for zero-rated VAT when physical exportation is evidenced and the goods are delivered to a foreign destination. Cross-border qualifying services, including software, ERP, CRM, cloud services, and other electronically supplied services, qualify for zero-rated VAT only when the recipient is a non-resident of Korea, the payment is received from sources outside Korea, title and control pass to a foreign customer, and the service is consumed outside Korea. For vertical cloud software sold both locally and cross-border from Korea, the taxpayer must prove the foreign end-customer location, the export destination of the service data flow, and the influx of foreign currency consideration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration issued through UNI-PASS (electronic export clearance report evidencing statutory exportation)
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing the Korean Chusik Hoesa as shipper/exporter and the foreign purchaser as consignee
Foreign exchange settlement confirmation issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the foreign customer
Commercial invoice and packing list consistent with the submitted Customs Export Declaration
Zero-rated VAT invoice or electronic tax invoice issued under the Korean e-tax invoice system and cross-referenced to the exported transaction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS, together with Korea Customs Service and Korean banking foreign exchange records, will cross-check zero-rated export claims against Customs Export Declarations, e-tax invoices, shipping or digital delivery logs, and foreign exchange settlement data. If the taxpayer fails to substantiate exportation, the foreign recipient status, lawful foreign exchange collection, or actual offshore consumption, the NTS will reverse the zero-rating and reassess 10% VAT on the full supply value. Additionally, the NTS will impose statutory penalty tax for negligent or fraudulent under-reporting, incorrect tax invoices, and failure to adhere to e-invoicing rules, with aggravated penalties and criminal referral to the prosecutor's office under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act where forged customs declarations or fabricated remittance evidence are discovered. The clawback extends to any input VAT credits previously claimed against the zero-rated supply, and paid VAT becomes immediately due with statutory interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA) and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA), with the Foreign Exchange Information System as the operational reporting gateway
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a de jure liberalised current account for trade and service payments; Korean won are fully convertible for legitimate operational flows, and no mandatory surrender of export proceeds is imposed. Capital account transactions including inbound equity investment, intercompany debt, securities and derivatives are subject to real-time reporting and, in certain cases, prior declaration through a licensed foreign exchange bank to the Foreign Exchange Information System. For a vertical ERP/CRM cloud company, the dominant cross-border flows are software licence fees, subscription revenues, subcontractor payments and intercompany royalties; these are treated as current account items when bona fide and underlying economic substance is demonstrated. Profit remittance to a foreign parent is freely permitted after submission of audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates from the Korean National Tax Service, and compliance with corporate governance documentation. The KRW floats with occasional BOK smoothing intervention; there is no layered approval licence for ordinary commercial transactions; however, practical hurdles include document-heavy validation of beneficial ownership, strict deadlines for reporting foreign receipts, and a legal prohibition on relying on unlicensed offshore fintech EMIs as the primary collection account for Korean revenue. The assessor must also distinguish capital from current account for each FX operation to avoid triggering the post-audit penalty regime under FETA.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement exists in South Korea. Exporters must receive all foreign currency due under an export or service agreement through a domestic licensed foreign exchange bank and must report receipt of each export value to the bank within 5 business days under FETA. Foreign currency may be held in a resident foreign currency account or converted to KRW voluntarily at market rates, but the underlying customs declaration or service export contract must be matched to the receipt. For software-related services, the documentation includes the signed contract, the SK-505 service export filing where applicable, and corresponding invoice/settlement instruction.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable as a primary banking rail for a Korean Chusik Hoesa. Korean financial regulation confines deposit-taking and foreign-exchange business to locally licensed banks. Offshore fintech EMIs holding an e-money or payment institution licence in another jurisdiction are legally barred from maintaining won-denominated corporate accounts or executing onshore FX for Korean entities without a local banking joint venture or a licensed bank umbrella. Stripe Billing and Direct Debit can be used as payment gateways, but funds must ultimately settle into a licenced Korean Tier-1 bank account. A global EMI may be used for non-Korean revenue streams, yet any Korea-sourced revenue or intra-Korea treasury needs a bank-account path. The onboarding compliance team should therefore always start with a domestic Tier-1 bank, and a foreign policy EMI only as a supplementary instrument for USD/EUR receipts where the customer is physically located outside Korea.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean AML and Financial Transaction Reports Act rules require verifiable identification of the statutory representative and ultimate beneficial owner. In practice the named director(s) must appear physically at a designated corporate service branch of the chosen Tier-1 bank, or provide a notarised Power of Attorney granting a Korea-resident signatory authority, with the original corporate registration documents apostilled/notarised. Some banks such as Hana and Woori offer a remote consular-opening desk for non-resident directors, but the waiver is discretionary and conditional on an initial video-bank interview, supplemental source-of-funds questionnaire, and submission of a certified Korean translation of all corporate documents. For a newly formed Chusik Hoesa with a wholly foreign UBO, the safest execution is a face-to-face meeting in Seoul or Busan during entity registration, followed by a local signatory appointment to facilitate ongoing account monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid creation of a dormant but capitalised local shell entity: a Chusik Hoesa with zero staff, soon to receive inbound foreign direct investment and then issue high-value software invoices to an overseas parent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the parent's certified global tax residence certificate, audited financial statements for the last two fiscal years, a concrete Korean staffing and office-expense budget, a lease agreement for a co-working space in Korea, a written business plan detailing target vertical clients in ERP/CRM, and at least three signed beta-client letters of intent or purchase orders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) holding 100% of the shares and having no Korean credit or tax history, appearing only through a local nominee officer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a passport copy notarised by the Korean consulate in the UBO's country of residence, an apostilled certificate of incorporation and register of directors from the parent jurisdiction, a board resolution authorising the account signatories, a private-side-dependent-beneficiary declaration, and a source-of-funds letter from the UBO's overseas banking institution demonstrating lawful accumulation of the capital injection amount.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment mismatch: an initial USD injection is quickly followed by an outbound payment to an unrelated foreign entity for so-called 'cloud licence fees' before any Korean revenue appears.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a milestone-based software sub-licence agreement with scope description, an itemised invoice containing the service period and maintenance code, the SK-505 service export filing or equivalent, the internal transfer-pricing policy with comparable arm's-length pricing benchmarks, and a project delivery timeline signed by the Korean engineering lead.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Receivables first appear from Stripe Billing or Direct Debit processors settling through an offshore EMI account rather than a licenced bank, creating geographic and ownership mismatches under Korean FX reporting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the Stripe/Direct-Debit verification letter confirming legal ownership and settlement routing, a board-approved treasury policy stating that gross Korean revenue must be collected through the domestic bank account within 30 days, records of monthly reconciliation transfers from the EMI to the Korean bank, and a resident director attestation with duplicated refund and dispute controls.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound share capital from the overseas parent must be wired to a designated Foreign Exchange Bank under the bank's FDI code 'Foreign Direct Investment' (FETA classification 320100). The transferring bank must file a foreign direct investment declaration with the Ministry of Economy and Finance through the Foreign Investment Support System (FISS) before or upon receipt. The funding channel is standard SWIFT MT103 with the explicit purpose code embedded in the wire narrative. After receipt, the bank issues a 'certificate of foreign direct investment', enabling registration of the Korean entity as a Foreign-Invested Company. Korean won are then released to a domestic operating current account at the spot exchange rate. For intercompany loans, a separate loan facility with a mandated rate and repayment schedule must be filed under FETA to prevent regulatory recharacterisation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Software subscription royalties, partner commissions, infrastructure fees and consulting disbursements should use SWIFT MT103 messages with the appropriate International Service Trade purpose code (e.g., 22600 for software implementation, 20400 for IT services). Each payment must be backed by a signed contract and an itemised invoice archived for at least 5 years under FETA. Commercial letters of credit may be used for large enterprise licence deals, but are uncommon in cloud software; documentary collections are rarely used. Domestic payroll and corporate tax payments are executed through the local Korean payment rails (Hometax/Jury-O and the Financial Settlement System), not through cross-border SWIFT.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore Korean won forward contracts (deliverable) against USD, EUR, JPY, limited to the value and tenor of the underlying export/service receivables or payables as evidenced by the corporate cash-flow forecast

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) may be used only through overseas branches of Korean licensed banks for hedging unsettled non-KRW receivables, with a clear prohibition on entering into NDFs without real underlying exposure

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for converting the notional and interest rate of a USD-denominated intercompany loan into KRW, provided the swap is designated as a hedge of the repayment liability and documented under IFRS 9

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and tax payment (corporation tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company, by March 31; a 1-month extension is available for qualifying companies under the Framework Act on National Taxes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalty of 20% of the payable tax; daily overdue interest at the statutory rate of approximately 0.022% per day accrues from the day after the due date; chronic delinquency can trigger asset seizure, business registration cancellation, and judicial dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local income tax surtax return and payment (10% surtax on corporate tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government tax authority (si, gun, or gu) via Wetax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the corporate income tax return deadline, being March 31 for a calendar-year taxpayer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfaithful-report penalty, non-filing penalty of up to 20%, daily late-payment interest at the statutory rate, and local tax seizure and property disposition for prolonged non-payment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-annual value-added tax returns and payments for software, cloud, and CRM service supplies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half (January-June) filed by July 25; second half (July-December) filed by January 25 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge, dishonest-report penalty, daily default interest at approximately 0.022% per day, and enforced collection actions by the NTS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit and submission of audited financial statements with the independent auditor's report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the electronic disclosure system (DART)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year companies, audited financial statements must be approved by the annual shareholders' meeting by March 31; the audit report must be filed with the FSS/DART within the statutory deadline for the external audit report, which in practice aligns with the AGM approval cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, failure to appoint an auditor, deliver audit reports, or file audited statements may result in administrative fines, disciplinary referrals, public disclosure, and supervisory intervention by the FSS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general shareholders' meeting with approval of financial statements, dividend decisions, and director appointment actions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company internal governance organ; minutes kept at the registered office and, for listed or large corporations, disclosed via FSS/DART
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual general meeting must be held within 3 months of fiscal year-end, i.e., by March 31 for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance exposes directors to shareholder derivative liability and administrative fines under the Commercial Act; unresolved governance failures can trigger court-led dissolution for a dormant or non-compliant corporation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent CPA audit is compulsory for a Korean Chusik Hoesa under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies if at fiscal year-end the company has total assets of at least KRW 12,000,000,000; additional criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree may require an audit based on total assets, total revenue, and employee headcount. Mandatory audit also applies if the company is a listed or publicly traded issuer, if it belongs to a designated large business group subject to the Monopoly Regulation and Fair Trade Act, or if it is a financial company or other entity required to be audited under separate financial statutes. For Korean companies, the balance-sheet threshold is the primary statutory trigger; a standalone annual turnover or headcount threshold applies only when the Enforcement Decree extends the audit requirement to lower-asset companies using those metrics.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) are required for listed companies and apply to companies that are subject to external audit; non-listed entities may apply Korean GAAP (K-GAAP) when not required to use K-IFRS, but a consistently applied framework must be followed. Audits must be performed under Korean Standards on Auditing, which are aligned with International Standards on Auditing, and all audited financial statements must comply with the disclosure rules of the Financial Supervisory Service.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a public annual UBO declaration form for a standard Chusik Hoesa. Beneficial-ownership verification is performed primarily through AML/KYC procedures by banks, payment service providers, and financial intermediaries. A share transfer must be recorded in the statutory shareholder register to take effect against the company; there is no general 30-day government filing for a domestic transfer, but transfers involving non-residents must be captured in the applicable foreign-exchange reports and disclosed in the annual corporate income tax return where required. Companies in regulated or high-risk financial sectors must satisfy the FSS AML/UBO submission and monitoring rules.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 1,500 per year for a professional registered office, company secretarial, and domicile agent in Korea; lower for pure virtual office arrangements and higher for multi-jurisdictional CRM/cloud structures.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 25,000 per year for a certified CPA audit of a non-listed Korean software/CRM company that meets the audit threshold; small exempt entities may pay approximately USD 2,000 - USD 5,000 for a voluntary audit or agreed-upon procedures.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9%-24% progressive national Corporate Income Tax; plus 10% local income tax surtax on the national CIT, giving an effective combined range of 9.9% to 26.4%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Free Economic Zone and certain foreign investment incentives may reduce national CIT by 100% for 5 years and by 50% for the following 2 years; R&D expenditure tax credits and job-creation tax credits under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act; technology-transfer income exemption or 50% CIT reduction for SMEs; no general patent box for ERP/CRM software, but software R&D credits and facility investment credits are available

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 24 Corporate Tax Return, including the Corporate Tax Base and Tax Computation Statement, filed electronically on the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (www.hometax.go.kr); the companion Local Income Tax Return is filed simultaneously with the competent NTS Regional Tax Office
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; interim advance CIT prepayments are required in the middle of the fiscal year, generally due within two months after the close of the first six months
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, the annual corporate tax return and local income tax return must be filed by March 31 of the following year; if the return is prepared and signed by a qualified Korean tax agent, the filing deadline may be extended to April 30; no extension beyond four months after fiscal year-end is allowed

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the Chusik Hoesa, business registration number, tax office, fiscal year-end, industry code (ISIC 6201 / computer programming), primary business scope of vertical ERP/CRM cloud software, and foreign investor information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean entity is a domestic corporation for Korean tax purposes. Use the Korean business registration number, not the foreign parent tax number. Attach the foreign shareholder schedule so that future dividend payments can be mapped to the correct non-resident withholding rate and treaty claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Line 1 - Gross Revenue / Total Sales
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue from ERP/CRM software subscriptions, licenses, cloud hosting, implementation, consulting, maintenance, and support, stated net of value-added tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenue from cloud subscriptions generally must be recognized over time; realized license sales are recognized when control transfers. For Korean subsidiary selling to foreign affiliates, test whether prices are at arm's length; any undercharge to the head office is an upward transfer-pricing adjustment to be reported in Box 7.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs including acquired software licenses, cloud infrastructure costs, subcontractors, hosting fees, amortization of intangible assets, and direct labor assigned to software delivery.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to a non-resident related party for software licenses or cloud services are deductible only if supported by contracts, economically substantive services, and contemporaneous transfer-pricing evidence. A Korean entity that operates only as a low-risk service provider to the foreign parent should apply a documented cost-plus method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit less selling, general, and administrative expenses, including wages, rent, telecom, legal, accounting, and marketing costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany management fees and head-office overhead allocations must satisfy the benefit test and must be documented. Charges that are actually profit distributions to foreign shareholders are not deductible and must be added back in Box 7.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Line 4 - Non-Operating Income and Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, foreign exchange gains and losses, dividend income, asset disposal gains, impairment losses, and other non-operating items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to the non-resident parent may be subject to thin capitalization limits under the Corporate Tax Act and must be reduced for withholding of the 22% statutory domestic WHT before treaty relief is assessed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Line 5 - Net Income before Income Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book income before income tax per Korean IFRS or K-GAAP financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The amount must exactly match the separate-entity Korean statutory financial statements. Foreign parent consolidation adjustments, balance-sheet-only entries, or group revenue allocations are not accepted by the National Tax Service.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additions and deductions that reconcile book income to taxable income: non-deductible expenses, entertainment limits, tax-exempt income, depreciation differences, reserves, and transfer-pricing corrections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory add-backs include non-arm's-length royalties, excessive service fees, thin-capitalization interest, hybrid mismatch payments, and amounts paid abroad without proper Korean source withholding. The Korean subsidiary cannot deduct any foreign tax due on dividends paid by itself.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 / Line 7 - Taxable Income before Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book income after all tax adjustment schedules; this is the starting point for applying tax loss carryforwards and progressive rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the NTS applies an arm's-length adjustment to intercompany charges, the taxable income is increased and the taxpayer has no right to deduct the counterpart foreign tax unless the foreign jurisdiction grants a corresponding adjustment under the applicable Mutual Agreement Procedure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction for tax losses carried forward from prior years, subject to the 15-year period for fiscal years beginning on or after the current statutory regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Korean-resident losses can be carried forward. A foreign-parent loss cannot be used. Significant change in ownership or business identity may cause the loss carryforward to be denied when the Korean Chusik Hoesa ceases its active software business.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply progressive national CIT brackets: 9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% above KRW 200 million and up to KRW 20 billion; 21% above KRW 20 billion and up to KRW 300 billion; 24% above KRW 300 billion.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Then compute local income tax surtax at 10% of national CIT, making the effective top rate 26.4%. The local income tax return is filed on the same date. Non-resident shareholders cannot credit their foreign withholding tax against this Korean corporate tax liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 - Tax Credits, Interim Payments, and Refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for foreign taxes paid by the Korean entity, electronic invoice credits, early filing discounts, interim advance CIT payments, and advance withholding credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the Korean entity's own foreign-source tax credits are allowed. The foreign parent's WHT credits do not flow through. Any credit claimed for withholding on foreign sales must include the foreign TRC and detailed source-of-income schedules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or filing a false or unfaithful return triggers a 20% negligence penalty under the Framework Act on National Taxes; additionally, a 20% documentation and understatement penalty may apply for transfer-pricing adjustments under the International Tax Adjustment Act. Late payment accrues daily statutory delinquency interest. Criminal evasion through deliberate concealment is prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying imprisonment up to five years or a fine up to ten times the evaded tax, increased for repeat offenders. NTS may seize corporate assets, freeze bank accounts, blacklist large delinquent taxpayers, and cancel tax clearance certificates.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surtax on dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders, giving an aggregate statutory rate of 22%; applicable Korea tax treaties typically reduce the rate to 5% to 15% depending on the shareholder's ownership percentage and treaty-lite clauses
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident recipient must submit, through the Korean withholding agent, a completed Application for Tax Treaty Reduction or Exemption, a current Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign competent authority, a beneficial ownership declaration proving the recipient is not a conduit, evidence that the recipient has real economic substance for the relevant activities, and a statement that the recipient does not maintain a Korean permanent establishment through which the dividends are attributable; the withholding agent must file the treaty relief application with the NTS before or at the time of payment; if excessive Korean tax is withheld, the non-resident may file a request for correction within three years from the statutory deadline, and treaty MAP proceedings are available to resolve refund or double-taxation disputes.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest and royalty payments to non-resident related parties are statutorily subject to 20% national WHT plus 2% local income tax surtax (aggregate 22%) before treaty; applicable DTAs commonly reduce interest to 10% to 15% and industrial/commercial royalties to 10% to 15%; for vertical ERP/CRM cloud arrangements, characterization is critical because fees for cloud hosting, software as-a-service, and technical support may be treated as business profits rather than royalties if no Korean PE exists, while payments for the right to use copyrighted software or patents are royalty-like and remain WHT-assessable.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File documentation is required where the Korean entity has annual revenue of at least KRW 100 billion and cross-border related-party transactions of at least KRW 50 billion; Local File documentation is generally required where aggregate cross-border related-party transactions reach KRW 50 billion, with per-foreign-related-party thresholds of KRW 5 billion triggering file preparation; even below the main thresholds, the annual Report on International Related-Party Transactions (Statement of Overseas Related Party Transactions) must be filed with the CIT return and contemporaneous documentation should be kept for transactions above the simplified reporting thresholds.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea applies a substance-over-form doctrine under the Framework Act on National Taxes and OECD BEPS Action 6 LOB/PPT principles incorporated into Korea tax treaties; a Korean Chusik Hoesa claiming domestic deductions or treaty benefits must show real core income-generating activities (CIGA) in Korea, including actual ERP/CRM sales staff, cloud infrastructure decision-making, contract negotiation, software development, risk assumption, and local bank accounts; a pure conduit subsidiary with no economic substance cannot claim DTA relief and may have intercompany payments recharacterized as deemed dividends or Korean-source income subject to the full 22% withholding.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission or false invoicing of Korean-source ERP/CRM subscription revenue, recording personal expenses of foreign directors as company expenses, destruction of books and records, or deliberate repeated declarations of zero profit while paying large management fees to the foreign parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act imposes imprisonment up to five years or a fine up to ten times the evaded tax, with repeat offenders exposed to up to ten years; the Framework Act on National Taxes imposes a 20% negligent payment penalty plus daily late-payment interest; fraudulent VAT or cash-sale suppression can also trigger the VAT Act penal provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts and the NTS will look to the de facto controlling director; under Korean Commercial Act Articles 389 and 401, directors are jointly and severally liable for company tax liabilities caused by intentional or grossly negligent conduct; civil asset seizure, criminal imprisonment of responsible directors, travel bans and NTS delinquency blacklisting may be imposed, and the corporate veil is pierced where the company is used as a sham for tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing manipulation and missing TP documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying non-arm's-length royalties, cloud support fees, interest, or management charges to the non-resident parent; keeping the Korean entity in perpetual loss while the foreign group extracts all ERP/CRM profit; failure to prepare Master File, Local File, or contemporaneous comparability evidence; using fabricated service agreements without actual employees or operations in Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The International Tax Adjustment Act permits the NTS to adjust taxable income to the arm's-length amount, deny deductions for lacking substance, apply a 20% penalty on the underreported international transaction tax amount, and extend the statute of limitations; failure to produce TP documentation can result in a separate penalty and adverse evidentiary inference.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who order or approve fabricated transfer prices can be treated as secondary taxpayers when the company cannot pay, with personal liability for CIT, local surtax, and penalties; criminal prosecution for document forgery or tax avoidance can lead to imprisonment; the foreign parent's excessive payments may be reclassified as constructive dividends subject to 22% WHT, and directors face personal asset recovery and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and tax treaty abuse / failure of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Korean Chusik Hoesa as a letterbox company with no office, no employees, no independent decision-making, no Korean bank account, and no substantive ERP/CRM activities; using the company solely to access a Korea DTA and strip dividends or royalties at reduced rates while the beneficial owner lacks the legal or economic capacity to receive the income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS will disregard the shell entity under the substance-over-form GAAR provisions of the Framework Act on National Taxes, deny treaty benefits under LOB/PPT clauses, reclassify all reported service or royalty payments as Korean-source dividends or other income, apply the full 22% WHT plus interest, and impose a 20% unfaithful-return penalty; the tax authority may also cancel tax clearance and report the entity to the financial information disclosure system.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The directors and shadow directors who control the shell face piercing of the corporate veil, personal assessment for all unpaid taxes, civil restitution of diverted assets, Korean court-ordered travel bans and arrest warrants, and imprisonment for fraudulent misrepresentation; non-resident directors conducting Korean management without a work visa also face immigration bars and forced exit from Korea.
